paragraphs: A Mercedes-Benz M272 engine rebuild starts from £3,600, regardless of which of the six models it's fitted to - the price tier is set by the engine, not the badge on the boot. A full replacement engine and fitting service is also available.
Exact pricing depends on the condition of your existing engine and the parts required - submit your registration for a fixed-price quote within 30 minutes.

cards.title: Rebuilding Your
cards.body: Most engine suppliers sell you a used engine of unknown history and hope it matches. We rebuild the engine your Mercedes already has instead - strip it down, pressure-test it, and replace every worn or damaged component with updated OEM parts. You get a near-new engine with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty, without the compatibility risk of an unknown used unit. This is the option most M272 owners choose.

cards.title: Replacement
cards.body: If your existing engine is beyond economical repair, we also offer full engine replacement and fitting - sourced and fitted by our team, with the same 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

cards.title: Used
cards.body: In some cases, a matched low-mileage used engine is the right call - particularly if you need your car back on the road quickly and your existing engine's damage is extensive. We can source and fit these too, though most owners who ask about used engines end up choosing a rebuild once they understand the compatibility risk a used unit carries.

options.body: "Reconditioned" is the term many owners search for when they mean the same thing as a rebuild - a full strip-down, inspection, and replacement of worn parts rather than a straight swap. If that's what you're after, our rebuild service is exactly that.
"Refurbished" often describes the same process from a different angle - restoring your existing engine to full working condition rather than replacing it outright. Our rebuild covers this.

Some owners specifically search for a "remanufactured" engine, expecting a unit rebuilt to original specification with updated components. That's consistent with what our rebuild service delivers, regardless of which of the six M272-equipped models you drive.

faqLeft.q: What is the Mercedes-Benz M272 engine?
faqLeft.a: The M272 is Mercedes-Benz's 90-degree V6 petrol engine, produced from 2004 to 2015 in 2.5L, 3.0L and 3.5L capacities. It's fitted across 10 different Mercedes-Benz models.

faqLeft.q: Which Mercedes models use the M272?
faqLeft.a: CLK, CLS, E-Class, GLK, M-Class, R-Class, SL, SLK, Viano and Vito - see the full applications table above for exact variants and years.

faqLeft.q: Does the M272 differ between Mercedes models?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The specific ancillaries, mounting, and capacity (2.5L / 3.0L / 3.5L) differ by application, even though the base engine code is the same. We match by registration/VIN before confirming any rebuild or replacement.

faqLeft.q: Is an M272 from one Mercedes model compatible with another?
faqLeft.a: Not automatically. A 3.5L M272 from an E-Class isn't a drop-in match for a 3.0L M272 from an SLK - ancillaries, mounting and capacity all differ. We always confirm compatibility by registration/VIN.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes-Benz M272 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £3,200, regardless of which model it's fitted to. Exact price depends on condition and parts required - submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.
Yes. We work on M272 rebuilds across every model it's fitted to, replacing worn components as standard - including balance shaft components on pre-2008 engines.

faqLeft.q: What is the balance shaft issue on the M272?
faqLeft.a: On pre-2008 M272 engines (engine serial number < 2729..30 468993), the balance shaft sprocket gear can wear prematurely, causing timing issues and potentially catastrophic engine failure. We inspect and replace balance shaft components where required on every rebuild.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an M272 from an E 350?
faqRight.a: Yes. The M272 in the E-Class is one of the most common applications we see, across both the W211 and W212 generations.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an M272 from an ML 350?
faqRight.a: Yes. The M272 in the M-Class is one of the applications we work on regularly - the ML 350 from the W164 generation.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Mercedes-Benz M272 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Mercedes if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes - nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an M272 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most M272 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
